name: Kalka → Shimla
blurb: The toy train climbs into the Himalayan foothills through pine forest and more than a hundred tunnels. The longest is at Barog.

name: Mumbai → Goa
blurb: The Konkan Railway: paddy fields, waterfalls off the Western Ghats, and rivers wide enough to look like the sea.

name: Jodhpur → Jaisalmer
blurb: West into the Thar. Khejri trees, camel carts, sand ridges and wind turbines on the skyline, ending at a fort the colour of gold.

name: Mumbai → Pune
blurb: The Deccan Queen's climb up the Bhor Ghat: tunnels, viaducts and, in the rains, a waterfall around almost every bend.

name: Mettupalayam → Ooty
blurb: The Nilgiri Mountain Railway, a UNESCO heritage line, climbs on a rack track into the Blue Mountains through tea and eucalyptus.

name: Siliguri → Darjeeling
blurb: The Himalayan toy train winds through tea gardens and mountain fog up to Ghum, one of the highest stations in India.

name: Ernakulam → Kollam
blurb: Coconut palms, backwater canals and houseboats drifting beside the line through God's Own Country.

name: Madurai → Rameswaram
blurb: Across the flat Tamil coast and then out over open sea on the Pamban Bridge, India's first vertical-lift railway sea bridge.

name: Visakhapatnam → Araku
blurb: Up the Eastern Ghats in a glass-roofed coach: dozens of tunnels, coffee plantations and the Borra Caves station.
